title: Standards the specification relies on
description: Sources are normative only for specifically named adapters; UTV semantics supersede adapters where stricter, and differences MUST be disclosed (§17). spec/STANDARDS-MATRIX.md gives each standard's coverage class and acceptance test.

entities.title: ISO 8601-1 and ISO 8601-2
entities.summary: Dates, times, durations, intervals and repetitions; part 2 adds approximate, unknown and unspecified values, sets, seasons and selections.
entities.relevance: civil, instant, interval, recurrence, uncertain, set and selection map to it, native plus an adapter. ISO 8601-2 grammar must be checked against the licensed normative text before claiming it (OI-13).

entities.title: RFC 3339
entities.summary: Machine timestamps with offsets, including -00:00 for an unknown local offset.
entities.relevance: The instant and civil adapter must keep offset-unknown intent and fractional precision.
entities.citation: RFC 3339, Date and Time on the Internet: Timestamps

entities.title: RFC 9557
entities.summary: Named-zone annotations on timestamps, with criticality and offset semantics.
entities.relevance: civil.zone and offsetAssertion; the everyday API accepts a single [Area/Location] annotation and returns unsupported for any other.
entities.citation: RFC 9557, Date and Time on the Internet: Timestamps with Additional Information

entities.title: IANA tz database and TZif
entities.summary: Zone rules, including historical transitions; RFC 8536 defines the TZif file format.
entities.relevance: Zone rules are a registry dependency, pinned by version and content; the IANA database defines no geographic boundaries.
entities.citation: IANA Time Zone Database; RFC 8536, The Time Zone Information Format (TZif)

entities.title: RFC 5545 with verified errata
entities.summary: iCalendar recurrences, DTSTART/UNTIL, EXDATE/RDATE and DST behaviour; erratum 4271 treats nonexistent local times differently from invalid dates.
entities.relevance: The recurrence adapter must reproduce exact recurrence generation and §3.3.5 DST behaviour, as a policy separate from UTV's stricter default.
entities.citation: RFC 5545, Internet Calendaring and Scheduling Core Object Specification (iCalendar), with erratum 4271

entities.title: RFC 7529
entities.summary: Non-Gregorian recurrence rules: RSCALE and SKIP.
entities.relevance: Exact BYxxx/SKIP ordering is mandatory for the matching recurrence conformance claim.
entities.citation: RFC 7529, Non-Gregorian Recurrence Rules in iCalendar

entities.title: RFC 8984 (JSCalendar)
entities.summary: JSON events with recurrenceId, overrides and rule arrays.
entities.relevance: Moving an occurrence must keep its original recurrenceId.
entities.citation: RFC 8984, JSCalendar: A JSON Representation of Calendar Data

entities.title: RFC 8785 (JCS)
entities.relevance: The canonicalization profile produces deterministic UTF-8 JSON with JCS; large integers are strings, so no numeric rounding happens.

entities.title: RFC 2119
entities.summary: MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD and MAY.
entities.relevance: The specification's normative terms have their RFC 2119 meanings.
entities.citation: RFC 2119, Key words for use in RFCs to Indicate Requirement Levels

entities.title: W3C/OGC OWL-Time and ISO 19108
entities.summary: Nominal and numeric temporal positions, reference systems, temporal topology and interval relations.
entities.relevance: ordinal-position, temporal-reference, relation and temporal-graph; Allen's 13 relations and partial-order uncertainty.
entities.citation: W3C/OGC Time Ontology in OWL; ISO 19108 Geographic information — Temporal schema

entities.title: HL7 FHIR R5 Timing
entities.summary: Event-anchored schedules (meal and waking codes) and frequency obligations.
entities.relevance: event-relative and pattern: never invent concrete clock times from a frequency rule.

entities.title: OGC SensorThings, TimeseriesML and ISO 19156
entities.summary: Observations, samples and series, with phenomenon time apart from result time.
entities.relevance: series, sample and observation keep measurement and reporting times separate, and handle duplicate and missing samples.
entities.citation: OGC SensorThings API; OGC TimeseriesML; ISO 19156 Observations and measurements

entities.title: SQL:2011 temporal tables
entities.summary: Application time, system time and periods.
entities.relevance: assertion and event-history: bitemporal correction and overlap semantics.

entities.title: POSIX, UTC, TAI, UT1 and astronomical timescales
entities.summary: Epoch seconds, leap-second behaviour, Earth orientation, Julian Date and TT.
entities.relevance: instant, clock and temporal-reference: explicit timescales, leap tables and validity windows; POSIX seconds are not SI seconds across a leap second.
entities.citation: IEEE 1003.1 (POSIX); BIPM/CGPM and ITU-R resolutions on UTC; IERS

entities.title: Unicode CLDR
entities.summary: Locale data for formatting dates and times.
entities.relevance: Formatting (operation I3) depends on a CLDR data source, which no library ships yet.

sources.symbol: I. Getting values in and out

entities.title: EDTF
entities.summary: The Extended Date/Time Format: uncertain, approximate and unspecified dates, and slash intervals.
entities.relevance: An interchange adapter; the text form reads EDTF slash intervals, and EDTF qualifiers are not yet mapped (docs/.dev/backlog.json, edtf-qualifiers).
entities.citation: Library of Congress, Extended Date/Time Format (EDTF) Specification

entities.title: JSON Schema Draft 2020-12
entities.relevance: It validates shapes only; calendar correctness, graph consistency, registration and cross-field arithmetic need semantic conformance tests (DECISIONS item 18).
entities.citation: JSON Schema: A Media Type for Describing JSON Documents, draft 2020-12
